**Proposed mechanism:** POMGNT1 (HGNC:24311) —DISRUPTS→ dystroglycan processing pathway (GO:0035577); POMT2 (HGNC:9462) —DISRUPTS→ dystroglycan processing pathway (GO:0035577); dystroglycan processing pathway (GO:0035577) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal glycosylation of alpha-dystroglycan (HP:0030063); Abnormal glycosylation of alpha-dystroglycan (HP:0030063) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital muscular dystrophy (HP:0000015); Abnormal glycosylation of alpha-dystroglycan (HP:0030063) —LEADS_TO→ Brain anomalies (HP:0002059); Abnormal glycosylation of alpha-dystroglycan (HP:0030063) —LEADS_TO→ Eye anomalies (HP:0000479). Mutations in POMGNT1 and POMT2 disrupt the dystroglycan processing pathway, leading to abnormal glycosylation of alpha-dystroglycan, which in turn causes congenital muscular dystrophy, brain anomalies, and eye anomalies.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in POMGNT1 or POMT2 in affected individuals do not lead to impaired alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation, or that the identified mutations are common benign variants in gnomAD. _(variant: Exome sequencing data from gnomAD showing a high frequency (>1%) of pathogenic variants in POMGNT1 or POMT2.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared pathway disruption in dystroglycan processing offers a potential therapeutic target for both diseases, aiming to restore proper glycosylation or downstream signaling.
